decisions.reason: The fifteen-day express program sits close to the core offer and costs little to keep open, but it overlaps with the other express programs, so it is a candidate for consolidation.
The seventy-two-hour express option is cheap to maintain and its value is still uncertain, so keeping it open preserves upside despite possible later merging with Product D.
This European-approved fire-resistant exterior door extends a proven modular system with strong home-page visibility, so the investment is already committed and keeping it costs little.
The umbrella express delivery program has its own dedicated page, which signals commitment, and it is likely to absorb the narrower express options rather than be dropped.
The digital ordering platform is a strategic growth option for trade partners whose value is still unfolding, and its sunk setup costs favor keeping it.
Fire and smoke protection doors are core, certification-backed products with steady demand, so dropping this one would make little sense.
